nodes.description: Heterozygous nonsense variants in the third and last exon of PERP, p.Trp151* (c.452G>A or c.453G>A) and p.Tyr153* (c.459C>G), lie within two residues of each other. Because they sit in the terminal exon the mutant transcript escapes nonsense-mediated decay, and patient keratinocytes make a C-terminally truncated protein. The authors argue against haploinsufficiency: obligate heterozygous carriers of an N-terminal truncation are unaffected, PERP truncating alleles occur in control databases, and Perp heterozygous mice have no phenotype. Their favored model is a combined dominant-negative and neomorphic effect, which remains untested.
